title: Replacing a Whole-House Plumbing Trap: Cast Iron Removal and No-Hub Assembly

locations.name: Exterior excavation area near the house (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript references 'outside the last part of the excavation' and 'house trap removed', implying an exterior trench or excavation area rather than an interior location

summary: This Old House demonstrates replacing a whole-house plumbing trap by removing the old cast-iron trap, cutting and removing the surrounding pipe, and installing a new drain assembly using a No-Hub coupling. The segment shows cutting the soil pipe with a chain-type cutter, breaking a cast-iron fitting with a sledgehammer, removing old lead-and-oakum sealing, and assembling a new outlet with an angle fitting, cleanout, neoprene gasket, and No-Hub bands. A torque wrench is used to snug the bands without overtightening, and the installer measures and cuts replacement pipe to fit with proper pitch. The video emphasizes careful measurement, gasket handling, and pressure-tested connections while noting a long-term (quote) “100 years” durability of the No-Hub assembly. The content aligns with common retrofit practices for exterior house drain lines and trap replacements, with attention to sealing materials and proper hardware torque.

sections.title: Removing and cutting the old pipe
sections.description: The host introduces the soil pipe cutter (chain with blades) and demonstrates wrapping it around the pipe, snugging, and turning the ratchet to cut the pipe. A risk is noted that the pipe may be worn and could fail when cut.

sections.title: Disassembling the cast iron side and removing old sealant
sections.description: On the opposite side, a sledgehammer is used to break the cast-iron fitting. The old lead and oakum (oil hemp) sealing are described and then chiselled away to expose clean pipe.

sections.title: Installing the new drain assembly with No-Hub coupling
sections.description: With the old trap removed, the team assembles an angle fitting and a cleanout, joined by a No-Hub coupling. A neoprene gasket is seated and tightened with a torque wrench. Pipe length is measured and cut (6 inches on one end, ~8 inches on the other), the gasket is folded to fit, and the bands are snugged for a durable, long-lasting connection. The segment ends with notes about calling a drain company and the size of the tools needed for cleanup.
